Restorations are a specific method of finishing off and destroying whatever is supposedly being restored.
Why? Because they are acts of self-destruction.
Not of the Church or the state.
Not of past forms of freedom, nor of past forms of obligation and authority.
We put it in order. It falls apart. We put it in order again, and fall apart ourselves.
My reply to a German who wanted to be angry about the NZZ [Neue Zürcher Zeitung]:
Are we perhaps supposed to be angry at the distinguished tone of the NZZ, at Werner Kaegi’s call for resistance, or at the refined Monsieur Béguin?
Are we even supposed to start talking about Phariseeism?
Let us instead remember, in a spirit of universal kindness, the beautiful story of the distinguished Swiss gentleman.
A distinguished Swiss gentleman was sitting on the shore of the Swabian Sea. Then he heard the desperate cries of a drowning man:
The distinguished Swiss gentleman looked away indignantly and said:
“I can’t swim either, but you don’t hear me making such a fuss about it!”
Deeply moving: the young Hellingrath discovered Hölderlin around 1910, against Goethe. He discovered the hidden German—which is to say, the true German, the non-public German.
Today I discovered §247 in Hegel’s Philosophy of Right.
I am drawn to the hopeless, to those who fail, to the condemned.
There is no hidden Marxist motive behind this, or any other kind of hidden motive.
No desire to change the world.
The certainty of grace internalized, moved into the private interior, and yet at the same time secularized.
The end of fear and trembling over a good cup of coffee and a pipe of fragrant tobacco.
The return of a well-disguised sensual pleasure, after Luther and the Moravians had attacked security so fiercely as the true form of sensual pleasure.
“Where now is your pleasure?” asks the prophet of the miserable man who has been thrown out of his security.
“Where now is your trembling?” I ask this Quaker who has become a billionaire.

The date on the birth certificate of the modern just war, and of the union between its particular kind of justice and weapons of annihilation, the birthplace of the modern Bethlehem where the storms of steel are prepared, and at the same time the beginning of that era of international law which organized its four-year Epiphany at Nuremberg beginning in October 1945:
How tactful that the date was not 24 December 1910.
A letter from Mr Andrew Carnegie to the trustees of the Carnegie Endowment:
“I have transferred to you, as trustees of the Carnegie Peace Foundation, ten million dollars in mortgage-secured five-percent bonds, worth eleven and a half million dollars.
“You will use the income to abolish war, this stain upon our civilization.
“We no longer eat our fellow human beings; we no longer torture prisoners; we no longer plunder cities and destroy their inhabitants. And yet we still make war like barbarians.
“Only among wild beasts could this be excused in the twentieth century of the Christian era, because war is by its very nature criminal—la guerre est essentiellement criminelle.”
Answer: because it gives victory not to right, but to power. It is a crime—another new crime!—for a people to refuse arbitration.

(But the same text also contains the sentence: Le juge qui siège dans une cause où il est intéressé est discrédité jusqu’à sa mort: the judge who sits in a case in which he himself has an interest is discredited until his death.)
And the Secretary-General of this foundation for the criminalization of war was James Brown Scott! So in any case: here stands the cradle of the new fame of Francisco de Vitoria.
Here is the source of the new, modern doctrine of the just war.
Here, in the steelworks of Bethlehem.
I, in the loneliness of the man who runs ahead of everyone else, make discoveries of this kind at the risk of my life.

I find the polarity between the superman and the “non-human,” and the modern concept of an enemy who must be exterminated, in Karl Marx in 1844, in the introduction to the Critique of Hegel’s Philosophy of Right:
Criticism, when directed against Germany, “is not an anatomical knife; it is a weapon. Its object is its enemy, which it does not want to refute, but to destroy.”
Karl Marx at the age of twenty-six!
So: the destruction of the justus hostis, the legitimate enemy, from both sides.
From Bethlehem as well as from Moscow.

And in between them, a German fool receiving injections from the West who thought he could fight both a two-front war and two different kinds of war: a non-discriminating war in the West, and a discriminating war in the East.
The transition to the sea as the new element:
K. Marx, Riazanov I, p. 131: turning points in the development of philosophy.
When a divided world is confronted by a total philosophy, there is no reduction of its claims.
Instead there is a transition into another element.
Just as Themistocles, when Athens was devastated, persuaded the Athenians to abandon it completely and found a new Athens at sea, in another element.
I was the only one who demanded this for Germany and Europe: the conclusion of Land and Sea.
A transition to fire? Or to air?
In one of Alain’s Propos I found the following quotation: space is the image of our power, and time is the image of our powerlessness.
Whether the part about time is true, I leave open. But space is power. That is why the word Großraum—“great space”—caught on immediately, whereas we can speak of a “great time” but not of a Großzeit.
The essence of being is spatial being: location, space, and power. It is not temporal succession. It is presence—that is, space.
The fact that bodies could not pass through one another was space and power. That is precisely what is coming to an end.
The unlimited ability of waves to pass through everything is no longer power but influence.
“God is dead” means: space is dead.
(That is why the masses, despite all their fear for their own lives, display such incomprehensible indifference toward physical death and toward the destruction of their bodily form.)
In its place comes submission to forces.
Space is power made present, not force.
Time is neither one nor the other.
Forces are powers that have not yet been located.
Powers are forces that have been given a location.
Virgil, Horace—all of it littérature dirigée, directed literature; all of it engagée, committed literature.
Even the Eclogues are a hymn to Caesar.
What do those who call us traitors actually demand from us?
Trahison des clercs as the slogan of a supposedly existing pouvoir spirituel, a spiritual power.
Has nobody yet noticed the sheer arrogance of such slogans, and the brazen claim to a monopoly over humanity, which means the right to brand one’s opponent as inhuman and strip him of his rights?
How could “natural law” possibly fail to attract eager believers again and again?

Natural law: a few dozen completely contradictory demands; a heap of vague general clauses; basic concepts that are simply assumed—the concept of nature and the concept of law above all—without ever being clearly defined; a picture with a hundred different faces and a hundred wax noses.
How could something like that not win universal approval?
Again—as last week, on 3 August 1948—I am horrified by Karl Marx.

Fourth Thesis on Feuerbach, The German Ideology, p. 534: the self-division, the self-contradiction of the worldly foundation must itself be understood in its contradiction and therefore revolutionized in practice.
“So, for example, once the earthly family has been discovered as the secret of the holy family, the former must itself be destroyed in theory and in practice.”
Destroyed in theory and in practice. He wants to change things. And that means, first of all, destroying them.
Destroying them in theory and in practice.
Consolation: the destroyer destroys only himself. This is true above all of the destroyer of destroyers.
